120-elective-courses-15-credits: Chosen with your research supervisor; a few may be taken at other Québec or Canadian universities.
120-program-description: Nutrition and metabolism across the lifespan, with a focus on phytochemicals and food toxicants, food chemistry, safety, product development and food's effects on health. No dietitian licensure.
For careers in biotechnology, pharmaceutical or food industries, government labs and health communications, or further study toward research, medicine or dentistry.
120-required-courses-63-credits: All must be passed with C or better.
121-elective-courses-15-credits: You can take a few at any Québec university, or at Canadian or international ones with prior approval.
121-program-description: Nutrition and food at community and international levels: how diet, water, environment and infection interact. No dietitian licensure.
For government and NGO food and health agencies, development programs, the food sector and health communications, or further study in public health, epidemiology, research, medicine or dentistry.
123-program-description: How diet affects health and the mechanisms of inherited and acquired chronic disease, including nutrigenomics, nutrigenetics and biotechnology. No dietitian licensure.
124-program-description: How exercise and physical activity shape health and chronic disease prevention, on top of the nutrition core. No dietitian licensure. Similar careers and graduate paths to the other concentrations.
125-program-description: An introduction to metabolic nutrition to complement programs like Biochemistry, Biology, Physiology, Microbiology, Animal Science or Food Science.

24 credits, at least 18 not overlapping your main program, in sequence with C or better. Declare early in U2 and get your choices approved by the School's adviser. Plan ahead, since many 300+ courses have prerequisites and some don't run yearly.
No professional recognition, so it won't make you a dietitian, though it can help with postgraduate nutrition programs.
127-about-the-department-of-natural-reso: Sustainable management of ecosystems we depend on: wildlife and fish, insects, agriculture, soil, microbes, genomics, forests, landscape ecology, resource economics and policy. Graduate programs in agricultural economics, entomology, microbiology and renewable resources.

Teaches in the majors in Environmental Biology, Life Sciences, Environment, Sustainable Agricultural Systems and Agricultural Economics, and in specializations in Applied Ecology, Wildlife Biology, Microbiology and Molecular Biotechnology, Agribusiness, Environmental Economics, and Life Sciences (Multidisciplinary).
127-program-description: Agriculture relies on companies supplying farms and transporting, processing and marketing food. Combines agricultural science, agribusiness and Desautels courses. For Agricultural Economics majors only.
128-program-description: If it runs: apply in March or April of U2 with CGPA 3.3 and a supervisor, take 12 Honours credits on top of your major at B or higher, and graduate with 3.3.
129-complementary-courses-9-credits: With adviser approval, one introductory course each in accounting, statistics, and written or oral communication.
129-specialization-24-credits: Agribusiness, Environmental Economics or Professional Agrology. OAQ membership needs two of these.
129-program-description: Applied economics for sustainable development, the environment, and global food systems, with marketing, finance, farm management, public policy, ecology, resources and development.
129-complementary-courses-6-credits: With adviser approval, one introductory course each in statistics and in written or oral communication.
129-specialization-24-credits-2: Take Agribusiness or Environmental Economics. Agribusiness students can add Professional Agrology for Agribusiness, and OAQ membership requires both.
130-program-description: Basic biology of large mammals and birds, preparing you for most North American veterinary colleges, postgraduate biology and lab work.
130-program-description-2: How ecosystems work and how to manage them for agriculture, forestry, fisheries, protected areas and cities, using systems thinking and tools for handling complexity.
131-program-description: Apply in March or April of U2 with CGPA 3.3 and a supervisor; 12 Honours credits beyond your major and specialization at B or higher, 3.3 at graduation.
Biology, diversity and ecology from plants and vertebrates to insects, fungi and microbes, with strong field components, training ecologists, taxonomists, field biologists and ecosystem scientists.
132-honours-plan-a: 12 credits of Honours research in your major, chosen with the Program Director and supervisor.
132-honours-plan-b: 6 credits of Honours project and 6 at the 400 or 500 level, normally in the Faculty, chosen with the Program Director and supervisor.
132-specialization: At least one of 18–24 credits: Applied Ecology, Plant Biology or Wildlife Biology are designed for this major.
132-program-description: Biology and ecology of organisms from plants and vertebrates to insects, fungi and microbes, in their ecosystems and under environmental change. Lots of field work, using the Macdonald setting, to train ecologists, taxonomists and field biologists.
133-program-description: Environmental science and decision making with the economics of sustainable development, for careers in resource management and policy analysis. Agricultural Economics majors only.
133-program-description-2: Apply in March or April of U2 with CGPA 3.3 and a supervisor; B or higher in Honours courses and 3.3 at graduation. Your program's name then includes Honours.
A strong base in biological sciences for agricultural, environmental, health and biotechnology careers, or for postgraduate and professional study.
133-required-courses-45-credits: The Program Director may approve other statistics courses.
134-specialization: At least one of 18–24 credits: Animal Biology, Animal Health and Disease, Life Sciences (Multidisciplinary), Microbiology and Molecular Biotechnology, or Plant Science.
134-program-description: A strong base in biological sciences for agricultural, environmental, health and biotechnology careers. Top graduates may go on to research or to veterinary, medical and health programs.
134-program-prerequisites: See Minimum Credit Requirements. If you don't choose a specialization, you're given Life Sciences (Multidisciplinary) when you enter U2.
135-program-description: A wide choice balanced between fundamentals and applications, specialized or broad as you like, opening up bioscience industries and, with the right CGPA, postgraduate or professional schools.
136-program-description: Principles and applications of microbiology, with choices toward basic science or biotechnology. Leads to labs in universities, government and industry, pharmaceutical, fermentation and food industries, or further study.
136-program-description-2: Plants from cell to organism: structure, physiology, development, evolution and ecology, with labs at the Morgan Arboretum, Herbarium, Lods Research Centre, Horticultural Centre, greenhouses and field stations. A research project is possible.
Leads to graduate study or work in botany, mycology, molecular biology, ecology, conservation or environmental science.
137-program-description: Required for OAQ membership and taken only with the Agricultural Economics Major and Agribusiness Specialization. Covers agricultural law, professional conduct and work in agribusiness.
137-program-description-2: Agricultural law, professional conduct and work in agrology. Taken with the Sustainable Agricultural Systems Major; adding Field Crops and Horticulture, Global Food Security, or Livestock meets OAQ eligibility.
138-complementary-courses-18-credits: From one of the listed specializations, and you must be in the Sustainable Agricultural Systems Major.
138-program-description: Ecology and management of vertebrates and their environments, using the Avian Science and Conservation Centre, Arboretum, Stonycroft Wildlife Area, Molson Reserve and Ecomuseum.
139-program-description: Adds a social science view, knowledge of how the economy works, an understanding of the agri-food business environment, and analysis of agriculture's relationship with natural resources.
139-program-description-2: How ecosystems work and how to manage them for agriculture, forestry, fisheries, protected areas and cities, with systems thinking.
24 credits with C or better, at most 6 shared with your major (electives excluded).
